Published by
MBNO: Mamba-based neural operators for solving partial differential equations
Article preview
Abstract
Keywords
abstract:
Abstract
The recently released Mamba model leverages structured state space models (SSMs), incorporating hardware-efficient designs and selection mechanisms. The Mamba architecture demonstrates strong potential as a replacement for Transformer-based models across various tasks. In this work, we employ Mamba to train neural operators on infinite-dimensional spaces derived from partial differential equations. Using well-established theory on the Rough Path and Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space (RKHS), we theoretically demonstrate that the SSM-based models can replace Transformer-based models for approximating operators. Our empirical findings further show that Mamba consistently outperforms Transformer models across various tasks while achieving faster inference, highlighting the potential of the Mamba architecture to outperform Transformer-based models in various operator learning tasks.

  - heading "Introduction" [level=2]
  - generic: The Transformer architecture, introduced in Vaswani et al. [1], has significantly advanced machine learning across various tasks. However, its quadratic computational demands for sequences limit its practicality for large-scale or real-time applications. To overcome these constraints, variants such as linear Transformers [2], reformers [3], and structured state space models (SSMs) [4], [5] have been developed. In particular, SSMs reduce computational complexity compared to naive Transformers and offer improved memory efficiency and faster inference. Excelling across multiple modalities, including language, audio, and genomics, SSMs demonstrate substantial potential to replace Transformer-based models in diverse tasks.
  - generic: Recently, researchers have shown significant interest in solving physical problems using machine learning techniques such as Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) [6], [7] and operator learning [8], [9]. Operator learning, in particular, offers a promising alternative to traditional methods, such as the Finite Difference Method (FDM) or Finite Element Method (FEM), by reducing computational repetition. This reduction is achieved using trained models as the solution operator for a family of partial differential equations (PDEs). To this end, minimizing the model’s inference time is crucial when solving PDEs with trained models, as it enhances real-time responsiveness and operational efficiency.
  - generic: In this study, we investigate the effectiveness of the Mamba architecture [4] within the domain of operator learning, providing theoretical estimates and empirical evidence from experiment results. Our findings reveal that the Mamba architecture achieves better training outcomes than the existing Transformer-based models and significantly enhances inference speed. This improvement in performance and efficiency highlights the potential of Mamba as a powerful tool in scientific computing, with the possibility of replacing Transformers. This paper serves as an introductory exploration into the capabilities of SSM-based architecture, including Mamba, in solving physical problems using machine learning.
  - generic: In a related line of work, Zheng et al. [10] proposed the Alias-free Mamba Neural Operator, presenting structural results such as continuous–discrete equivalence and alias-free representations. Unlike their focus on structural properties, our MBNO framework provides rigorous theoretical guarantees for replacing Transformer layers with Mamba layers using Rough Path theory and controlled differential equations (CDEs).

  - heading "Discussion and conclusion" [level=3]
  - generic: This study introduces the Mamba architecture for solving PDEs in operator learning. Compared to existing Transformer-based models, it achieves enhanced accuracy and improved inference speed. The integration of selective state-space mechanisms significantly reduces computational overhead and boosts inference performance.
